original_test_intent: Verify that the intended BMC exposes a valid Redfish service-root document that can be retrieved successfully and contains no ambiguous duplicate JSON object keys or unintended duplicate root resource references under the project's definition of duplicate data.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware, Redfish version/schema and trusted endpoint; authenticate through a protected session with certificate validation; GET exactly `/redfish/v1` once; retain status line, response headers and the original response body bytes before parsing; validate content type and JSON syntax with a parser that reports repeated object keys; inspect required service-root metadata and links; apply the approved normalization rule to detect duplicate resource references without treating legitimate aliases or repeated values in different fields as duplicates; close the session without mutation.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies the required service-root field/link matrix and exact duplicate-data rule; the secure GET, raw parse and evaluation are fully automatable.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware, Redfish service version and expected service-root schema/profile
Required `@odata` metadata and root resource links with permitted OEM/optional fields
Definition of duplicate data: repeated raw object key, duplicate normalized resource URI, duplicate semantic member or another explicit rule
Trusted certificate/CA policy, protected credentials/session method and allowed response-header redaction
safety_requirements: Verify endpoint identity and certificate trust before authenticating
Keep credentials out of URLs, logs and process output; redact authorization/session headers
Capture raw body before any parser collapses duplicate keys
Issue only GET and do not follow unexpected cross-host redirects
Stop on wrong target, TLS/auth error, non-success status, malformed/truncated body, ambiguous duplicate rule or schema mismatch

Run duplicate-key-aware JSON decoding and approved resource-URI normalization
Validate required metadata/links and report every missing or duplicate finding
Do not weaken TLS, expose secrets, mutate Redfish state, guess duplicate semantics or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the target Redfish schema/profile and mandatory versus optional service-root members
Define duplicate scope, normalization and legitimate-alias exceptions
Approve certificate/authentication policy and sensitive-header redaction

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: GET `/redfish/v1` is the correct read-only operation, but `-k` weakens target identity and jq's ordinary object model cannot prove the raw JSON had no duplicate keys.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a TLS-validated, secret-safe Redfish client to save raw headers and body separately; run a duplicate-key-reporting JSON parser before normal schema/link validation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact service-root GET, successful-value and no-duplicate checks, Common scope and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate the raw HTTP representation, duplicate object-key semantics and decoded service-root link graph separately so a lossy parser cannot hide malformed source data.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds endpoint trust, status/content-type evidence, raw-byte preservation, explicit duplicate domains and profile-aware root-link checks.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Pretty-printed JSON only shows the parser's final object; many parsers silently keep the first or last repeated key, and identical values under distinct legitimate properties are not necessarily duplicates.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Redfish implementations may include OEM links or URI aliases, so semantic duplicate detection must be profile-specific while raw repeated object keys can be rejected unconditionally if project policy says so.

project_override_considerations: If 'header data' specifically means HTTP response headers rather than the JSON service root, engineering must add the required header matrix; the current Procedure's no-duplicate language targets returned data and the `/redfish/v1` document, so both HTTP and body are preserved without inventing acceptance fields.

Duplicate-aware parser/version and raw repeated-key report

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title's 'header data' is imprecise, but Procedure and Criteria coherently require retrieval of the Redfish service root and absence of duplicate returned data. Preserving both HTTP metadata and JSON avoids narrowing coverage.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2240 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00022-V001: approve the BMC/firmware Redfish version/profile and mandatory/optional `/redfish/v1` metadata/resource links; define 'no duplicate data' across raw repeated JSON object keys, normalized duplicate resource URIs, semantic members and permitted OEM aliases; state whether specific HTTP headers are also acceptance data, and approve TLS/authentication plus redaction policy.

review_improvement: Preserves the exact service-root read while making duplicate detection meaningful at the raw representation and schema/link levels instead of trusting a lossy pretty-printer.
independent_technical_reasoning: JSON permits parsers to accept repeated object names even though their interpretation is ambiguous, and jq normally exposes only the resolved object. Therefore the body must be inspected with a duplicate-aware decoder before ordinary parsing. 'Duplicate data' can also mean two root links resolving to the same resource, but identical strings in unrelated fields are not automatically defects. Separating raw-key, URI and schema checks produces a reproducible read-only oracle while retaining HTTP header evidence suggested by the title.
